c4isr_products.name: Spacetime
c4isr_products.description: Temporospatial software-defined networking (SDN) orchestration platform that models the time-dynamic position/orientation of satellites, aircraft, ships and ground stations and continuously plans, schedules and steers directional links (RF and optical) across space/air/land/sea networks; deployable as single-tenant customer-owned Kubernetes instances (cloud, on-prem, classified/air-gapped per company claim). Includes a Federation ('Spacetime Fabric') feature to broker interconnect between separately orchestrated networks.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: INPUT: network model (platforms, antennas, interfaces, ephemerides/motion, weather, link budgets), service requests and traffic-engineering policies via NBI; telemetry from devices via SBI. PROCESS: temporospatial link planning, beam scheduling, routing/SR-TE path computation, re-planning as geometry changes. OUTPUT: beam/radio/flow control schedules pushed to devices; computed paths; simulations. USER: network operations engineers at satellite operators and military SATCOM/transport organizations (e.g., DIU HSA, AFRL SDNX, Telesat Lightspeed).

c4isr_products.name: Tightbeam
c4isr_products.description: Free-space optical (laser) communications terminals (T170x fixed, G170x gimballed; 170 mm aperture) claimed at up to 100 Gbps with demonstrated ground-to-air links approaching 200 km; six terminal generations rooted in LLNL work; native Spacetime integration; optical ground-segment 'network as a service' announced as coming.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: INPUT: IP traffic and Spacetime schedule/pointing commands. PROCESS: laser link acquisition/tracking and high-rate optical transport. OUTPUT: point-to-point 100 Gbps-class links between land/air (sea/space announced). USER: transport-layer operators needing high-capacity, low-probability-of-intercept backhaul.

companies.exact_problem_solved: Directional (narrow-beam RF and optical) links between moving platforms constantly break as geometry, weather and terrain change; Spacetime automates the planning, scheduling and re-routing of those links across heterogeneous multi-orbit/multi-domain networks so operators can run 'networks in motion' without manual link engineering. Tightbeam supplies the high-capacity optical links themselves.

companies.apis_sdks_open_interfaces: FACT (HIGH): Spacetime publishes open, Apache-2.0 gRPC/Protocol Buffers APIs at github.com/aalyria/api: Northbound Interface (Model, Provisioning/SR-TE, Solution, Simulation, Permissions, Audit), Southbound/CDPI (bidirectional scheduling stream + telemetry export; reference Go agent), Federation/East-West (interconnect and transponder capacity brokering), plus a Status API; nbictl CLI; Go/Python packages; developer portal docs.spacetime.aalyria.com. Third-party audit (API Evangelist, Aug 2026) counts 45 proto files, 13 services, 182 RPCs; no REST/OpenAPI, no public pricing or self-serve sign-up; per-customer instance domains with self-signed RS256 JWT auth. NBI was under migration in 2026 (third-party integrator note to pin to v21.0).
